scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

In this scenario, the 18-year-old brother (you) was left in charge of his 7-year-old brother, and he made a decision to let him stay up late to watch a movie with friends. While it's understandable that you wanted to accommodate your brother's desire to spend time with you and your friends, it's also important to consider the potential consequences of letting him stay up late. The 7-year-old brother is described as sensitive to sleep deprivation, and it's clear that he was not in a good state the next morning. Your mom was upset with you for not enforcing bedtime, and you argued that your brother should know about consequences and that 2 hours of missed sleep is not a big deal. From a neutral perspective, I would say that you were not entirely in the wrong (NTA). Here's why: 1. You were left in charge, and you made a decision to let your brother stay up late. While it's not ideal, it's not entirely your fault that your mom left you in charge and didn't set clear expectations. 2. You did try to enforce bedtime initially, but your friend's influence and your brother's persistence made it difficult to do so. 3. You carried your brother upstairs and put him to bed, which shows that you were still taking care of him, even if you didn't enforce bedtime immediately. 4. You argued that your brother should know about consequences, which is a valid point. At 7 years old, children are still learning about cause-and-effect relationships and should be encouraged to take responsibility for their actions. However, it's also worth considering that you could have found alternative solutions to accommodate your brother's desire to spend time with you and your friends. For example, you could have: * Set a later bedtime for the movie night, but still ensured that your brother got some rest. * Involved your mom in the decision-making process to get her input and ensure that everyone was on the same page. * Found ways to make the movie night more engaging and interactive for your brother, so he wouldn't feel left out. Ultimately, the decision to let your brother stay up late was a complex one, and it's not entirely clear-cut. However, I would say that you were not entirely in the wrong (NTA), but you could have handled the situation better with more consideration for your brother's needs and your mom's expectations.
